encounter_greeting.text: Halt, {player}. I am {persona} of {my_faction}, and this road is ours. Stand aside or answer to me for every step you take here.
So it is you, {player}. I see your colours and I do not like them. {persona} of {my_faction} marks this ground as ours, and I will not be moved from it.
Greetings, ser {player}. I am {persona}, sworn to {my_faction}. Pass in peace and we shall have no quarrel today.
Ser {player}, what a joy to meet you on the open road! {persona} of {my_faction} has long hoped our paths would cross.
Friend {player}, {persona} of {my_faction} is glad of your company. Our hall has room for an honest sword such as yours.

encounter_threatened.text: You would demand {gold} of me, {player}? No banner of mine bows to extortion. Draw your steel and learn what a sworn house will pay.
Think you that I would part with {gold} for the asking, ser {player}? You will find my people harder to buy than to threaten.
Ser {player}, {gold} is a heavy sum to name before any gate has opened. State your terms plainly and I shall weigh them honestly.
Dear {player}, surely you jest? Threats sit ill upon a friend. Speak plainly and I will hear you out before any gold changes hands.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: Very well, ser {player}. I accept your oath of alliance. Let our banners stand together against {enemy_faction}, and let no one call me faithless.
I will take your hand against {enemy_faction}, ser {player}. Keep your word and I shall keep mine. That is the whole of my bargain.
Gladly, friend {player}. A blade like yours beside mine will sit well at the edge of {enemy_faction}'s lands. Do not let {rival} spoil this pact.

encounter_alliance_no.text: I refuse you, {player}. A house that has bled once does not trust so lightly, and I shall not take your oath while you stand so near to {rival}.
Keep your offer, {player}. I will not bind my house to a name I cannot trust, and certainly not while {rival} still walks at your side.
I thank you for the offer, ser {player}, but I must decline. My oath is bound elsewhere for now. Perhaps another day.
I must decline, ser {player}. My house has a debt of blood to settle first, and no pact can rest upon such grief.
It grieves me to refuse you, dear {player}. My oath to a fallen bannerman weighs too heavily on me to take on another bond yet. Forgive me.

captured_by_player.text: So you have me in chains, {player}. Take your {gold} from my house if you must, but know that {my_faction} will remember this humiliation.
Bind me as you like, ser {player}. Every chain you lay upon me is a debt I will repay with interest, in the name of those who went before me.
You have won this field, ser {player}, and I yield to your steel. Name your ransom of {gold} and let us conclude this honourably.
Fortune favours you today, ser {player}. {my_faction} shall pay what is owed, {gold} to free us both from this sorry field.
Ser {player}, you fought fairly and I bear you no ill will. My ransom is {gold}, though I would sooner yield to a worthy foe than to any other.

released_by_player.text: Ser {player}, you let me walk free without ransom. I shall not forget such mercy, and my house owes you a true debt.
Ser {player} loosed me without a ransom and asked nothing in return. Mercy such as that is rare on this road.
You loosed me without ransom, {player}, and I do not thank you for it. I would rather have met you properly in the field. Mark that.
You let me go, ser {player}. Mercy has a weight of its own, and I shall carry it with honour.

player_left_my_faction.text: You have turned your back on {my_faction} and taken up with {faction}, ser {player}. A banner pledged and then broken is a shameful thing.
{player} has forsaken {my_faction} for {faction}. Oaths sworn in fair weather are always the first to rot.
Ser {player}, I hear you have gone over to {faction}. Each house must choose its road, but I grieve to see your name leave ours.
Dear {player}, I know the heart that drew you from {my_faction}. Still, I will remember the comrade you were to us.

war_declared.text: Hear me, all of Ormerath! {my_faction} takes up arms against {enemy_faction}, and the debt shall be paid in full!
The horns have sounded. {my_faction} and {enemy_faction} are at war, and I shall see every blade of ours do its duty.
{enemy_faction} has earned our steel this day. {my_faction} will not sheathe until the account is settled.
Let no one doubt it: {my_faction} will not yield one step to {enemy_faction} while I still draw breath.

fought_alongside_player.text: Ser {player}, {troop_count} of our men stood fast beside yours against {enemy_faction}. I shall sing of this field to my grandchildren.
That was a battle worth the telling, ser {player}. Your {troop_count} fought like lions beside us. I am in your debt.
{player} and I held the line with {troop_count} blades against {enemy_faction} today. A fine morning's work for the saga.
We have bled together with {troop_count} soldiers against {enemy_faction}, ser {player}. That blood binds us, at least for today.
Glory to {player}! Our {troop_count} stood as one against {enemy_faction} and the field is ours. The fallen shall be remembered.

encounter_farewell.text: Begone, {player}. Our paths have crossed and I have no wish to see your face again soon. Go with what little honour you carry.
Ride on, {player}. Mark this meeting, for the next will be settled with steel and not with words.
Fare well, ser {player}. May your road be kind and your banner stay high.
Farewell, dear {player}. Do not let the road forget you, and come to our hall whenever your path turns this way again.
Go in good stead, friend {player}. The sky grows late, but my sword and my word remain yours.

ambient_chatter.text: The rain has come down on {town} like a judgement from heaven. I pity every merchant who must sell in it.
Has anyone passed through {village} lately? I hear the roads beyond it are muddy enough to swallow a cart whole.
A fine evening to ride out from {town}. The hills look as proud as I feel, which is saying a great deal.
Some bard should write a saga about the bridges of {village}. Surely they have seen more battles than most kings.
Every sunrise I count the days since my oath, and every day I find I am still owed a reckoning.
